column5: Criterion 6 requires every criterion checked; hiding criteria is wrong against ticket-check's reading.
Criteria 5 and 7 allow a free-text not-shown reason; slashes in it are not paths.
Marker inside a fence is plain text; one sane reading, wrong against criterion 6.
Not-shown mark belongs to the entry's own line; continuation-line match is a parser bug.
Oracle ticket-check ends the section at part-naming headings; script reads criteria from another part.
Unclosed opener hides later criteria; oracle reads text, criterion 6 needs every criterion checked.
Criteria 5 and 6 require evidence that exists under verify directory; second citation unchecked.
Entry rule must match the criteria indent rule; indented entry falsely reports missing evidence.
Oracle has a fenced-item rule; fence body must not count, one sane reading.
Oracle ends the section at a bare hash heading; plain divergence with one sane answer.
Ticket never says where the final check transcript is cited when every criterion is not-shown.
Criterion 2: a project must never name a credential; bare and camelCase names slip through.
Criterion 3 exports each lane's own session; a decoy match exports another thread's.
Session identity must come from the top-level id; nested id winning is a plain bug.
Ticket never says what happens when several records match a thread: newest, refuse, or all.
Self-test must not depend on inherited environment; any reading requires a hermetic test.
Criterion 2 never allows a credential name; secretKey is plainly one and slips through.
Pre-existing launch line; any reading needs the flow's event-stream path protected from env overrides.
Code contradicts its own documented boundary; stale sentence or wrong comparison, either way a fix.
Criterion 3 exports the lane's own session; suffix match on another thread's record is wrong.
Ticket never says whether an explicitly empty --project falls back to discovery or is refused.
Verifying a decoy repo is wrong under any reading; a missing environment guard.
Ticket never says the helper's exit when the gate passes but cleanup partly fails.
A failed install hidden behind a green gate is wrong under any reading.
Ticket never names where a scratch checkout lives; tmpdir versus repo parent are both reasonable.
verify.sh pm() already defines the package-manager order; install detection ignoring it is a plain gap.
Missing guard; verify.sh already bounds gates at 1800s, so mirroring it is the sane answer.
Install and gate must use the same package manager; lockfile decides, one sane answer.
Criterion 5 forbids verifiers for surfaces not given; an unknown folder passing contradicts it.
